evidence.description: public internal(set) static var current = make(for: .current)

candidates.explanation: The 'current' property is declared as 'public internal(set)', which is a contradiction. 'public' makes the property accessible to other modules, while 'internal(set)' restricts the setter to the current module. In Swift, 'public' properties must have 'public' setters to be accessible outside the module.
candidates.title: Contradictory Access Control

candidates.explanation: The 'make(for:)' method uses 'queue.sync' to access a property that is not being modified or accessed in a thread-unsafe manner within this scope. Since 'locale.withLanguage' is a read-only operation on a value type, the dispatch queue adds unnecessary overhead and potential for deadlocks.
candidates.title: Unnecessary Synchronization

evidence.description: public internal(set) static var current = make(for: .current)

candidates.explanation: The 'current' property is initialized using 'make(for: .current)'. However, 'Locale.current' is a dynamic property. If 'current' is intended to represent the system language, it may not update automatically when the system settings change, as it is only initialized once.
candidates.title: Static Initialization of Dynamic Value
